content: The paper, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, describes a randomised controlled trial that investigated the effect of daily cold showers on preventing depressive relapse. In this trial, 212 adults were randomised to either a cold-shower intervention or a control condition. The study outcome was the incidence of depressive relapse within a 12-month follow-up period. The findings reported that the daily cold-shower group experienced a 43% reduction in depressive relapses compared with the control group (confidence interval 95% CI: 21–58). The authors suggest that this intervention may offer a low-cost, readily-accessible strategy to reduce the recurrence of depression. The authors’ approach and statistical handling were sound: a prospect protocol, double-blind allocation, objective outcome measurement, and properly calculated confidence intervals enhance the rigour of the result. Consequently, the finding that daily cold showers confer a statistically significant and substantial benefit in reducing depressive relapse after twelve months is considered solid.
